national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for sensitising Urban Local Bodies to the challenges arising from urbanisation, including population growth and future water requirements, and suggested organising similar Chintan Shivirs for Urban Local Bodies. Mr Modi today chaired the valedictory session of the two-day National Departmental Summit on Water, organised by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. He called for greater adoption of water-saving technologies. He also suggested dedicated exhibitions and workshops, including exposure to global best practices, to enable Indian manufacturers and stakeholders to develop and scale efficient solutions. The prime minister appreciated the intensive two-day deliberations and emphasised that the actionable and time-bound action points emerging from the Summit should be pursued through a continuous process of review and learning. He suggested that the Summit should not remain a one-time exercise and called for a continuous process of review and follow-up. Emphasising Jan Bhagidari, Mr Modi suggested promoting “Jal Utsav” to create greater awareness among people. Prime Minister called for making de-silting a regular programme and developing clear criteria and SOPs for de-silting. On dam safety, he stressed rigorous preparedness before every monsoon, adherence to prescribed precautions and creating awareness among school students, including through suitable incorporation in educational curricula. The prime minister further called for strengthening knowledge and capacity on water management and governance in universities and higher educational institutions. He suggested structured inter-State study-visits involving public representatives, officials and farmers to facilitate practical learning and replication of successful interventions. The prime minister called for robust water data governance, with water-sector data brought together, systematically managed, analysed and effectively utilised. He recommended the use of AI for data collection and analysis through a uniform format. He also stressed anticipatory and integrated planning to address water scarcity through suitable utilisation of treated water for agriculture and industrial purposes.

national_raw_news.title: 50 mins ago | National 47 Retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra appointed as first CEO of Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Kshetra Trust
national_raw_news.content: In Uttar Pradesh, Former Commander of Western Air Command, Retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra is appointed as first CEO of Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Kshetra Trust in Ayodhya today. The appointment was announced after the meeting of trust held at Maniram Das Chhawani in Ayodhya under the chairmanship of trust president Mahant Nritya Gopal Das. The CEO will be responsible for overseeing the administrative functioning of the Trust and handling key operational responsibilities related to the Shri Ram Temple complex. Trust’s interim general secretary Krishna Mohan informed about the appointment of three new members, which include Madan Mohan Pandey, a senior advocate from Ayodhya; Mahesh Bhagchandka of Delhi; and retired principal Dr Nirmala Yadav from Shikohabad. New CEO of trust, Former Commander of Western Air Command has also played a key role in Operation Sindoor. He retired on April 30, 2026. He is also a recipient of Ati Vishisht Seva Medal and Vishisht Seva Medal. A three-member search committee was constituted on July 6 to select the CEO after allegations of donation theft at the Shri Ram temple. The committee comprises retired Justice Pramod Kohli, retired Lieutenant General Vishnukant Chaturvedi and Suresh Haware. More than five thousand five hundred applications were received for the post of CEO.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 29 Talks on trade, defence, technology and energy high on agenda during Belgium PM’s first vi...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister of Belgium Bart De Wever, will arrive in New Delhi a short while from now on a three day visit to India. Prime Minister De Wever is being accompanied by Belgian Minister of Defence, Theo Francken. This will be Prime Minister De Wever’s first visit to India since taking office in February last year. He will hold bilateral talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi tomorrow to discuss the entire spectrum of bilateral relations, as well as regional and global issues of mutual interest. The visiting dignitary will also deliver a keynote address at a Confederation of Indian Industry business event, in the context of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement. Our correspondent reports that the visit will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the India-Belgium partnership and advance cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, defence and security, and renewable energy. This is the first visit by a Belgian Prime Minister to India in two decades marking a significant new phase in India-Belgium relations. The visit reflects the continued momentum of high-level exchanges between India and Belgium. It will also reinforce Belgium’s important role in strengthening India-EU relations. Belgium is an important economic partner for India in Europe. Bilateral trade reached over 13 billion dollars in 2025-26. Diamond trade, with Antwerp as a major global diamond hub, remains a significant component of bilateral commerce. The Belgian Prime Minister is also scheduled to visit Mumbai on 4th September, highlighting the strong economic foundations of the partnership. His planned visit to the Bharat Diamond Bourse underscores the importance of the diamond trade in bilateral relations and opportunities for further cooperation in the sector. The presence of Belgium’s Minister of Defence and Foreign Trade, along with a delegation of Belgian defence industries, will provide an opportunity to advance cooperation between Indian and Belgian defence industrial ecosystems.

national_raw_news.title: India’s Kidambi Srikanth & Tanvi Sharma advance to second round of China Open Tournament 7 hours ago 263
national_raw_news.content: In Badminton, India’s Kidambi Srikanth and Tanvi Sharma advanced to second round of China Masters Super 750 tournament with straight-game victories in respective Singles’ events in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province. Men’s Doubles duo, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, and the mixed doubles pair, Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto also moved to the next round. In Men’s Singles, 2021 world championships silver-medallist, Srikanth defeated Chinese Taipei’s Chi Yu Jen 21-16, 21-15 in the opening match. The former World Number One will next face World Number 9 Victor Lai of Canada. However, Lakshya Sen, a 2021 world championships bronze-medallist, was knocked out of the tournament after going down against Victor Lai, 14-21, 7-21. In Women’s Singles, Tanvi overpowered Denmark’s Amalie Schulz 21-16, 21-17. The 17-year-old from Punjab, who won her maiden BWF World Tour title at the Taipei Open last month, will face Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki in next round. In Men’s Doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty registered a 21-11, 21-16 win over Malaysia’s Junaidi Arif and Kang Khai Xing. The Asian Games gold medallist pair will next take on the Popov brothers, Christo and Toma Junior of France. Mixed Doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto defeated Thailand’s Tonnakorn Saeheng and Tonnicha Saeheng 21-8, 21-9. The duo will meet Chinese Taipei’s Liu Kuang Heng and Hsu Yin-Hui next.

national_raw_news.title: Domestic markets end low extending losing streak for three consecutive session 4 hours ago 521
national_raw_news.content: Benchmark domestic equity indices ended around half a per cent lower today, extending their losing streak to three consecutive sessions. The Sensex declined 374 points to close at 76,570, while the Nifty fell 141 points to settle at 23,914. In the broader market, the Nifty Midcap 100 index slipped half a per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 index declined 0.4 per cent. Elevated crude oil prices, rising global bond yields and future inflation concerns dented Dalal Street sentiment. Earlier, the markets opened with a gap down amid negative global cues. Both indices traded within a narrow range and remained under pressure throughout the day. However, they pared some of their losses after the closing auction session. In the Sensex pack, 20 out of 30 companies logged losses. Among the top laggards, Asian Paints, HDFC Bank, Mahindra and Mahindra declined 1.6 per cent, HCL Tech dropped one and a half per cent and Bharat Electronics Limited lost 1.3 per cent. In contrast, Adani Ports climbed 1.6 per cent, Bajaj Finance, PowerGrid, NTPC gained one per cent and Titan added 0.7 per cent. In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 18 out of 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top underperformers, Auto declined 1.7 per cent, IT declined 1.2 per cent and Insurance as well as Capital Goods dipped 1.1 per cent. In contrast, Utilities rose 1.4 per cent, Housing Finance as well as Energy gained 0.7 per cent and Power added half a per cent. The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2560 companies declined, 1799 advanced and 217 remained unchanged.

national_raw_news.title: Uttar Pradesh and Germany discuss trade, investment, technical cooperation and expansion of MSMEs 1 hour ago 42
national_raw_news.content: In Uttar Pradesh, a delegation from Germany paid a courtesy visit to state MSME Minister Bhupendra Singh Chaudhary today. During the meeting, the delegation and the minister held detailed discussions on trade, investment, technical cooperation, and the international expansion of MSMEs between Uttar Pradesh and Germany. Minister Bhupendra Chaudhary said that bilateral trade between India and Germany stands at approximately 31.01 billion dollars. He added that Germany accounts for approximately 19.8% of UP’s total exports to the European Union. Uttar Pradesh exports more than 404.20 million dollars annually to Germany, with readymade garments, leather products, footwear, carpets and auto components being the major items. The meeting informed that the Indo-German Gateway Program is a structured 12-month program being implemented in cooperation with Germany’s Innovation Hub Rhein-Main and GIBA. Under this program, selected MSMEs and startups will receive assistance in establishing legal companies in Germany, understanding the market there, and connecting directly with foreign buyers. German delegation appreciated UP’s strong infrastructure and business environment. They stated that the program would not focus only on large companies, but would also select promising MSMEs and startups with a clear vision. Minister Bhupendra Chaudhary invited German entrepreneurs to the fourth UP International Trade Show, to be held in Greater Noida from September 25 to 29. He said this partnership would provide a strong foundation for long-term cooperation in trade, technology, investment, and skills.

national_raw_news.title: Bombay HC orders CBI probe into death of former Manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput 2 hours ago 70
national_raw_news.content: The Bombay High Court today ordered a CBI probe into the death of Disha Salian, former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, and pulled up the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years. A division bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and Ranjitsinha Raja Bhonsale said that an investigation cannot drag on for an inordinately long period, emphasising that a central agency probe was necessary to ensure a proper and substantive investigation into the matter. The court observed that the investigation carried out by the police raises more questions than it answers. Disha Salian, who briefly worked as manager of actor Sushant Singh Rajput, died on June 8, 2020, after falling off the 12th floor of a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. The city police then registered an Accidental Death Report. A week later, the actor was also found dead in his apartment on June 14, raising speculation that there could be a link between the two deaths. The high court asked the CBI to register an FIR and record the statement of Disha’s father, Satish Salian, but clarified that no person shall be treated as an accused until and unless there is sufficient material gathered against them during the probe.
